recall_prompt: Say how you would compute this triple product — say which part you do first.

steps.label: Find b×c
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. The bracket is on the right, so b×c is computed first — brackets before the outer product, exactly as in arithmetic.
steps.memory_tip: The bracket is on the right, so b×c first — brackets before the outer product, as in arithmetic.
lines: Given a = i − j − 6k, b = i − 3j + 4k, c = 2i − 5j + 3k
To find a×(b×c), first find b×c:

recall.must_convey: That the bracket b×c is computed first, giving 11i + 5j + k.
accept: first work out b cross c which is eleven i plus five j plus k
the bracket comes first so compute b cross c
find the inner product b cross c before crossing with a
modata bracket lo unna b cross c cheyyali, eleven i plus five j plus k
compute the term in the bracket first

steps.why: The outer product cannot start until the bracket is a single vector. Brackets first is the same rule as in ordinary algebra.
common_mistakes: Computing a×b first because it is written first.
Sign slip on the j term, where the minus is part of the expansion.

steps.label: Cross a into the result
steps.margin_note: The other half. Put a on the first row and the bracket result on the second — the order in the question is a×(…), so a comes first.
steps.memory_tip: a on the first row and the bracket result on the second, matching the order in the question.

recall.must_convey: That a is crossed into the bracket result, with a on the first row, giving 29i − 67j + 16k.
accept: cross a into that with a on the first row to get twenty nine i minus sixty seven j plus sixteen k
the answer is twenty nine i minus sixty seven j plus sixteen k
take a cross the result of the bracket
a ni first row lo petti cross cheste twenty nine i minus sixty seven j plus sixteen k
the final vector is twenty nine i minus sixty seven j plus sixteen k

steps.why: Cross multiplication is not commutative, so the row order matters: swapping the rows would give exactly the negative of this answer.
common_mistakes: Putting the bracket result on the first row, which negates everything.
Dropping the minus that sits in front of the j term.

insider_note: Work the INNER bracket first — a×(b×c) is not the same as (a×b)×c and the two give different answers. Compute b×c, then cross a into that result.
